channel.title: FXStreet Forex & Commodities News
channel.description: Real-time Forex News and the latest trading updates. Stay updated on the latest news about currencies and commodities markets.

item.title: Natural gas: Price downside limited – Commerzbank
item.description: Norman Liebke at Commerzbank argues that European gas prices may see only limited further declines despite a brief 8% drop on US–Iran diplomatic headlines.

item.title: Gold consolidates as Iran diplomacy hopes clash with hawkish Fed expectations
item.description: Gold (XAU/USD) consolidates on Tuesday as traders weigh fresh Middle East headlines while the broader geopolitical backdrop remains tense. At the time of writing, XAU/USD trades around $4,328 after rebounding from an intraday low of $4,291 during European trading hours.

item.title: Canadian Dollar: USD strength keeps CAD weakness in focus - Scotiabank
item.description: Scotiabank strategists Shaun Osborne and Eric Theoret note that the Canadian Dollar (CAD) is largely unchanged, with Governor Macklem’s comments leaving the Bank of Canada (BoC) outlook broadly consistent with the latest policy statement.

item.title: Fed’s Collins: More restrictive policy should help inflation return to 2%
item.description: Boston Federal Reserve (Fed) President Susan Collins said in a LinkedIn post on Tuesday that she supported last week’s interest-rate hike and sees a somewhat more restrictive policy stance as appropriate to bring inflation sustainably back to the Fed's 2% target.

item.title: Risk sentiment improved and Oil prices fell: Why the US Dollar is still holding firm
item.description: The US Dollar (USD) remains on a solid footing following a hawkish Federal Reserve (Fed) interest rate decision and persistent hawkish rhetoric from Fed officials.

item.title: Euro remains cautious as Middle East headlines, Fed outlook drive sentiment
item.description: EUR/USD is little changed on Tuesday as the US Dollar (USD) gives back earlier gains following fresh diplomatic signals surrounding the war between the United States (US) and Iran.

item.title: Silver edges lower as demand-led inflation keeps Fed tightening risks in focus
item.description: Silver (XAG/USD) declines 0.38% on Tuesday and trades around $65.85 at the time of writing.

item.title: Oil: Supply shock keeps prices elevated – NBC
item.description: National Bank of Canada's (NBC) Ethan Currie reassesses Oil pricing, highlighting persistent Middle East disruptions, depleted reserves and refined product shortages.

item.title: India: Growth, liquidity and policy response – DBS
item.description: DBS Group Research economist Radhika Rao assesses India’s strong start to FY27, with high-frequency data pointing to around 7% growth in 2QFY and full-year FY27 growth of 7.3% year-on-year.

item.title: Bank of England: Modest insurance tightening path – Deutsche Bank
item.description: Deutsche Bank Research’s UK economists Sanjay Raja and Maui Brennan have shifted their BoE base case from no hikes to two 25bp moves, in November and February. They argue Bank Rate is already restrictive, inflation is largely energy-driven, and second‑round effects remain limited.

item.title: Japanese Yen: Turning point with BoJ shift – OCBC
item.description: OCBC strategists Sim Moh Siong and Christopher Wong argue that intervention risks and a more hawkish Bank of Japan (BoJ) are key for the Japanese Yen (JPY).

item.title: Australian Dollar steadies as Middle East diplomacy takes focus
item.description: AUD/USD trims part of its earlier losses on Tuesday as traders assess fresh diplomatic signals surrounding the war between the United States (US) and Iran, weighing on the US Dollar (USD).

item.title: US Dollar: Hawkish fedspeak backs upside risks – ING
item.description: ING’s Francesco Pesole notes the Dollar started the week strongly despite lower Oil prices and firmer global equities, helped by hawkish remarks from Federal Reserve officials Austan Goolsbee and Alberto Musalem that supported US front-end rates.

item.title: Australian Dollar: RBA seen hiking as inflation risks build – Standard Chartered
item.description: Standard Chartered’s Nicholas Chia now expects the Reserve Bank of Australia (RBA) to raise the cash rate to 4.60% at its 29 September meeting, revising a previous call for a hold. Chia cites recent RBA messaging focused on upside inflation risks and resilient economic momentum.

item.title: US ADP Employment Change 4-week average increases to 20K
item.description: Private-sector hiring in the US has gained some pace in early September. According to the NER Pulse, the weekly companion to the ADP National Employment Report, companies added an average of 20K jobs per week in the four weeks ending September 5.

item.title: British Pound: Fiscal squeeze risks dovish BoE – BBH
item.description: Brown Brothers Harriman’s (BBH) Elias Haddad highlights that GBP/USD remains under 1.3400 as United Kingdom (UK) fiscal policy turns more restrictive. Rising borrowing has eroded fiscal headroom, pressuring Chancellor John Healey to tighten via taxes and spending cuts.

item.title: Euro: Softer versus Dollar as ECB tightening meets French risks – MUFG
item.description: MUFG’s Lee Hardman reports the Euro (EUR) is trading on a softer footing against the US Dollar, with EUR/USD near the bottom of its 1.1400–1.1800 range.

item.title: EUR/GBP Price Forecast: 100-day SMA blocks recovery as momentum remains subdued
item.description: EUR/GBP edges higher on Tuesday as the British Pound (GBP) remains under pressure across the board, weighed by concerns over the UK’s deteriorating fiscal outlook and the Bank of England’s (BoE) reluctance to raise interest rates while several major central banks have moved toward tighter policy.

item.title: Swiss Franc rallies on risk appetite while SNB threatens with FX intervention
item.description: The Swiss Franc (CHF) extended its recovery against the US Dollar (USD) on Tuesday, favoured by lower Oil prices amid hopes of a new round of US-Iran negotiations, which has prompted the Swiss National Bank (SNB) to launch an intervention warning.

item.title: US Dollar: Modestly stronger into year-end – OCBC
item.description: OCBC strategists Sim Moh Siong and Christopher Wong highlight that the US Dollar (USD) stayed resilient despite improved risk appetite, supported by hawkish Federal Reserve (Fed) commentary that limited the drop in US front-end yields.

item.title: Indian Rupee gains sharply as US-Iran diplomacy hopes pressure oil prices
item.description: The Indian Rupee (INR) rises significantly against the US Dollar (USD) on Tuesday.

item.title: Hungarian Forint: Key 360 area supports consolidation against Euro – Societe Generale
item.description: Societe Generale analysts describe EUR/HUF as consolidating above the 360 area after an interim low near 348 in June. The pair is capped by the 200-day moving average at 370/371, with a breakout above this zone needed to confirm a larger up-move.

item.title: Japanese Yen: Overbought rally faces 158.40 cap – UOB
item.description: United Overseas Bank’s (UOB) Quek Ser Leang and Lee Sue Ann note that USD/JPY remains supported after testing the 157.30 area, with short-term price action expected to stay within a 156.90–157.80 range.

item.title: Japanese Yen recovers against US Dollar as oil prices correct sharply
item.description: The Japanese Yen (JPY) claws back its early losses and turns slightly positive against the US Dollar (USD) during the European trading session on Thursday, with the USD/JPY pair dropping 0.2% to near 157.00.

item.title: Canadian Dollar hesitates as Oil falls amid Hormuz reopening talks
item.description: The Canadian Dollar (CAD) trades practically flat against the US Dollar (USD) on Tuesday as the risk appetite triggered by Tehran’s proposal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz has offset the decline in Crude prices.

item.title: South African Rand: SARB hike and hawkish tone – Commerzbank
item.description: Commerzbank’s Volkmar Baur expects the South African Reserve Bank (SARB) to deliver a 25 basis point rate hike after surprising markets by holding rates in July.

item.title: Gold Price Forecast: XAU/USD approaches $4,300 after rejection at the $4,400 area
item.description: Gold (XAU/USD) trades lower for the second consecutive day on Tuesday, extending its decline to levels below $4,320 during the European session, as the recovery attempt from last week’s low was capped at $4,400.

item.title: Hungarian Forint: NBH stance supports carry appeal – ING
item.description: ING’s Frantisek Taborsky expects the National Bank of Hungary to pause its mini easing cycle at 5.50% and possibly outline a two-step cut in its inflation target from 3.0% to 2.0%.

item.title: Silver price today: Silver falls, according to FXStreet data
item.description: Silver prices (XAG/USD) fell on Tuesday, according to FXStreet data. Silver trades at $65.61 per troy ounce, down 0.78% from the $66.13 it cost on Monday.

item.title: US Dollar: Fed tightening keeps upside risks – BBH
item.description: Brown Brothers Harriman’s (BBH) Elias Haddad notes the US Dollar (USD) is extending gains after the latest hawkish Federal Reserve (Fed) hike, even as reopening prospects for the Strait of Hormuz temper the move and weigh on Oil.
